chapter: Leading his own band in New York
title: Club Afrique and Barrel of Fun sidemen; Shorty Scott
summary: Musicians in his bands, and trumpeter Shorty Scott robbing a Philadelphia club.

story.theme_name: Gangsters, bootleggers and rough clubs of Prohibition
story.community_name: Gangsters, bootleggers and the Prohibition-era clubs

blocks.x: Yeah.
So Club Afrique wasn't these guys; it was different guys?
No, no, no. I had Miller--
Oh, a good trumpet player.
I had him on trumpet down there and this Herbie--
Herbie Goodwin?
Herbie Goodwin on Piano. If I'm not mistaken, I think the guy who played on bass with me was--a light fellow who was with me out here--
Not John Brown?
No, not John Brown.
This is before the Barrell of Fun? Club Afrique is before the Barrell of Fun?
Yeah, it was before the Barrell of Fun.
The Barrell of Fun you
I had Bobby Moore on trumpet.
Who did you have on saxophone?
Willard Brown.
Oh, Willard Brown was at Club Afrique?
No, Willard Brown was at the Barrell of Fun.
Did you have Shorty Scott?
I was going to say, for a while I had Shorty Scott. He was a clarinet player and a saxophone player, but he was a crook.
I don't know, I don't know too much about him.
He stayed with me for a while and over in Philadelphia he stayed on, after the club closed he was in the men's room or someplace and robbed the place. So I found myself without a trumpet player.
